newsitem.title: USA: TransCanada has rupture on main gas line.
newsitem.headline: TransCanada has rupture on main gas line.

text.p: TransCanada Pipelines Ltd said Thursday one of its 30-inch diameter natural gas pipelines ruptured late Wednesday near Vermillion Bay in western Ontario, forcing the company to shut the line.
The company said it was rerouting gas through an adjacent line and did not expect the outage to affect deliveries.
A company spokesman said he did not have the exact figures for the volume of gas flowing through the line at the time of the rupture.
The entire TransCanada natural gas system, comprising three trunklines, is currently carrying about 6.5 billion to 6.7 billion cubic feet a day (bcf), said company spokesman Tony McCallum.
"There was a rupture, the gas ignited, the fire burned itself out," McCallum said, adding the break occured about 2230 CST.
He said the cause of the leak was still unknown and declined to speculate on when the line might be repaired and reopened.

"Traffic was disrupted on the nearby Trans Canada highway and two people are currently under medical observation for injuries sustained as they left the scene," the company said in a separate statement. It did not elaborate.

Traders said the outage was behind a surge in natural gas prices on the NYMEX, where the January futures contract for delivery at Henry Hub, La., hit an early session high of $3.530 per million British thermal units, up $0.027 from Wednesday's close.
